q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 350B of the Constitution, the reports of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities are caused to be laid before each House of Parliament, and sent to the Governments of the States concerned, by the President.
2. The Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar of the Department of Official Language is awarded for original book writing in Hindi on specified subjects.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Under Section 8 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act vests in the Central Government.
2. The first Hindi newspaper 'Udant Martand', published from Calcutta in the year 1826, was edited by Pandit Jugal Kishore Shukla.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Articles 350A and 350B were inserted in the Constitution by the Constitution (7th Amendment) Act, 1956.
2. Kannada was accorded the status of a 'classical language' by the Government of India in the year 2008.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 351 of the Constitution, Hindi shall be enriched, without interfering with its genius, by assimilating the forms, style and expressions used in Hindustani and the other languages of India specified in the Eighth Schedule.
2. Meetings of the Town Official Language Implementation Committee (Nagar Rajbhasha Karyanvayan Samiti) are normally held twice a year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Official Language Commission to be constituted under Article 344 of the Constitution consists of a Chairman and other members representing the different languages specified in the Eighth Schedule.
2. The Sahitya Akademi gives its awards for literary works in 24 languages.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Official Language Rules, 1976 apply to the whole of India except the State of Tamil Nadu.
2. The celebrated Hindi poem 'Madhushala' was composed by Harivansh Rai Bachchan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Official Languages Act, 1963 came into force on 26th January, 1965.
2. 'Rashmirathi', the celebrated Hindi poem based on the life of Karna, was written by Ramdhari Singh Dinkar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. In-service Hindi training was made compulsory for Central Government employees by the Presidential Order of 1960.
2. The celebrated Hindi poem 'Jhansi ki Rani' was composed by Subhadra Kumari Chauhan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the State of Punjab is placed in Region 'B'.
2. The first Hindi daily newspaper, 'Samachar Sudha Varshan', was published in the year 1854 from Calcutta.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the State of Karnataka is placed in Region 'C'.
2. The 'Tar Saptak' (1943), the anthology that heralded modern experimental poetry in Hindi, was edited by Agyeya.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 348(3) of the Constitution, where a State Legislature has prescribed a language other than English for use in Bills introduced in, or Acts passed by, that Legislature, a translation of the same in English, published under the authority of the Governor in the Official Gazette of the State, shall be deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in the English language.
2. 'Urvashi', the celebrated Hindi epic poem for which its author received the Jnanpith Award, was written by Ramdhari Singh Dinkar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Under Section 6 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, a translation in Hindi of an Act passed by the Legislature of a State in a language other than Hindi, published in the Official Gazette of the State under the authority of the President, shall be deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in Hindi.
2. Sumitranandan Pant was awarded the Jnanpith Award for his poetry collection 'Chidambara'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Chapter IV of Part XVII of the Constitution is titled "Special Directives".
2. The first Indian leader to address the United Nations General Assembly in Hindi was Atal Bihari Vajpayee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Munshi-Ayyangar formula on the official language is named after K. M. Munshi and N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar.
2. The Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (Central Institute of Hindi) at Agra was established in the year 1960.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Official Languages (Amendment) Act, 1967 gave statutory effect to the assurance that English would continue to be used as long as the non-Hindi speaking people required it, an assurance originally given by Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru.
2. 'Rajbhasha Bharati', the quarterly journal devoted to the Official Language and its implementation, is published by the Department of Official Language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The three-language formula for school education was first recommended by the Education Commission (Kothari Commission), 1964-66.
2. The office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities was set up in the year 1957.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 350 of the Constitution, every person is entitled to submit a representation for the redress of any grievance to any officer or authority of the Union or a State in any of the languages used in the Union or in the State, as the case may be.
2. The websites of Central Government offices are required to be maintained in Hindi and English, i.e., in bilingual form.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 29 of the Constitution, any section of the citizens residing in India having a distinct language, script or culture of its own shall have the right to conserve the same.
2. Software packages procured for use in Central Government offices are required to have the facility of working in Hindi as well, i.e., bilingual (Hindi-English) capability.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Manuals, codes, forms and other procedural literature of Central Government offices are required to be printed and published in diglot form, i.e., in Hindi and English.
2. The Acharya Mahaveer Prasad Running Shield is awarded to the best (Adarsh) Division for excellence in implementation of the Official Language Policy in Regions 'A' and 'B'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. A Town Official Language Implementation Committee (Nagar Rajbhasha Karyanvayan Samiti) is chaired by the senior-most Central Government officer (head of office) in the town, nominated for the purpose.
2. Hindi Diwas was celebrated for the first time in the year 1953.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 347 of the Constitution, where the President directs that a language spoken by a substantial proportion of the population of a State shall be officially recognised, such recognition may be for the whole or any part of the State and for such purposes as he may specify.
2. The Central Hindi Training Institute was established in the year 1960.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Chapter III of Part XVII of the Constitution comprises Articles 350 and 351.
2. The Official Language Resolution, embodying the policy for the progressive use of Hindi for the official purposes of the Union, was adopted by Parliament in the year 1968.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Odia was accorded the status of a 'classical language' by the Government of India in the year 2013.
2. The office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities functions under the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The first Official Language Commission (Kher Commission), appointed in 1955, submitted its report to the President in the year 1956.
2. The Twelfth World Hindi Conference was held at Port Louis (Mauritius).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The standard of the Praveen course of the Hindi Teaching Scheme corresponds broadly to the Matriculation (Class X) level.
2. The headquarters of the Hindi Sahitya Sammelan, a leading organisation for the promotion of Hindi, is located at Prayagraj.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Fort William College at Calcutta, associated with the development of Hindi prose, was established in the year 1800 by Lord Wellesley.
2. Modern Hindi has evolved from Shauraseni Apabhramsha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Sahitya Akademi, India's national academy of letters, was established in the year 1954.
2. 'Dhruvaswamini', the celebrated Hindi play, was written by Jaishankar Prasad.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Under the three-language formula, the three languages to be studied in the Hindi-speaking States are Hindi, English and a modern Indian language, preferably one of the southern languages.
2. Under the three-language formula, the three languages to be studied in the non-Hindi speaking States are Hindi, English and Sanskrit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Article 350 from Article 350A of the Constitution?

options.A: Article 350 deals with facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage, while Article 350A entitles every person to submit a representation for the redress of grievances
options.B: Article 350 entitles every person to submit a representation for the redress of any grievance to any officer or authority of the Union or a State in any of the languages used in the Union or in the State, as the case may be, while Article 350A makes it the endeavour of every State and every local authority to provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage to children belonging to linguistic minority groups, the President being empowered to issue directions to a State for securing such facilities
options.C: Both the Articles deal only with the appointment of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
options.D: Article 350 provides for the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, while Article 350A deals with the development of Hindi

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Praveen from Pragya under the Hindi Teaching Scheme?

options.A: Both the courses correspond broadly to the Matriculation (Class X) level
options.B: Praveen is the final prescribed course for clerical staff, while Pragya corresponds broadly to the middle (Class VIII) level
options.C: Praveen corresponds broadly to the primary (Class V) level, while Pragya is the course prescribed beyond Praveen for advanced proficiency
options.D: Praveen corresponds broadly to the middle (Class VIII) level and is undergone after Prabodh, while Pragya corresponds broadly to the Matriculation (Class X) level and is the final prescribed course for clerical (ministerial) staff

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Acharya Mahaveer Prasad Running Shield from the Acharya Raghuveer Running Shield on Indian Railways?

options.A: The Acharya Mahaveer Prasad Running Shield is awarded to the best (Adarsh) Division for excellence in implementation of the Official Language Policy in Regions 'A' and 'B', while the Acharya Raghuveer Running Shield is awarded to the best (Adarsh) Division in Region 'C'
options.B: The Acharya Mahaveer Prasad Running Shield is awarded to the best (Adarsh) Division in Region 'C', while the Acharya Raghuveer Running Shield is awarded to the best (Adarsh) Division in Regions 'A' and 'B'
options.C: Both the shields are awarded only to Zonal Railways, and not to Divisions
options.D: Both the shields are awarded only to Adarsh stations and Adarsh workshops

q: Which one of the following statements relating to the scripts used for writing Indian languages is FALSE?

options.A: The Gurmukhi script, in which the Punjabi language is written, was standardised by Guru Angad Dev
options.B: The Ol Chiki script, invented for writing the Santhali language, was invented in the year 1925 by Pandit Raghunath Murmu
options.C: The script of the Malayalam language has evolved from the ancient script known as Grantha
options.D: The Kashmiri language is officially written in the Devanagari script

q: Which one of the following statements relating to the safeguards for linguistic minorities under the Constitution is FALSE?

options.A: The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is appointed by the President under Article 350B
options.B: Under Article 350A, it shall be the endeavour of every State and every local authority within the State to provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage to children belonging to linguistic minority groups
options.C: The office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities functions under the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs
options.D: The reports of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities are caused to be laid before each House of Parliament, and sent to the Governments of the States concerned, by the President

q: At a railway station, the application forms meant for use by the public are printed in Hindi and English only, the regional language of the area being omitted altogether. Under the Official Language Policy, the correct position is that such forms for public use are required to be printed in:

options.A: Hindi and English only, as printed at the station
options.B: Three languages — the regional language, Hindi and English

q: A Central Government office maintains its website in English only, on the ground that all its officers work in English. Under the Official Language Policy, the correct position is that the website of the office is required to be maintained in:

options.A: English only, as maintained by the office
options.C: Hindi and English, i.e., in bilingual form
options.D: The regional language of the State where the office is located

q: The Governor of a State, with the previous consent of the President, authorises the use of Hindi in the proceedings of the High Court of the State under Article 348(2) of the Constitution. A judgment of that High Court is thereafter delivered in Hindi, on the ground that the same authorisation covers judgments as well. The correct position is:

options.A: The authorisation under Article 348(2) does not extend to any judgment, decree or order of the High Court, the use of Hindi for judgments requiring a separate authorisation under Section 7 of the Official Languages Act, 1963
options.B: The judgment is in order, the authorisation for proceedings covering judgments, decrees and orders as well
options.C: The judgment is in order only if a Hindi translation of the judgment is also issued
options.D: The judgment is in order only in a State located in Region 'A'

q: A Central Government office spends 40 per cent of the total amount spent by it on purchase of books for its office library on Hindi books and claims to have complied with the Annual Programme target for purchase of books. The correct position is:

options.A: The claim is in order, at least 30 per cent of the amount being required to be spent on Hindi books
options.B: The claim is in order, at least 25 per cent of the amount being required to be spent on Hindi books
options.C: The claim is in order only if the office is located in Region 'C'
options.D: The claim is not in order, at least 50 per cent of the amount spent on purchase of books for office libraries being required to be spent on Hindi books

q: At a check point in a Central Government office, a press communique covered by Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 is presented for despatch in Hindi only. The correct course of action is:

options.A: To despatch it in Hindi, Hindi being the Official Language of the Union
options.B: Not to let the document leave the office unless it is issued in both Hindi and English
options.C: To despatch it in Hindi and send the English version a week later
options.D: To translate it into English at the check point and despatch the English version alone

q: An employee passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 61 per cent marks. The cash award admissible to him is:
An employee passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 71 per cent marks. The cash award admissible to him is:
An employee passes the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 96 per cent marks. In this case:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 95 per cent marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible only if he also passes the Hindi stenography examination
options.C: He becomes entitled to personal pay for a period of 24 months
options.D: A cash award is admissible to him, the prescribed threshold for the typewriting examination being 90 per cent or more marks

q: A candidate appears in the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and attains a speed of 82 words per minute. The correct position is:

options.A: He fails, the prescribed speed being 100 words per minute
options.B: He passes, the prescribed speed for passing the examination being 80 words per minute
options.C: He fails, the prescribed speed being 90 words per minute
options.D: His result is withheld, speed alone being insufficient for passing

q: An employee aged 41 years, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: He must undergo the training, in-service Hindi training being compulsory for an employee who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi and has not attained the age of 45 years
options.B: He is exempt, in-service Hindi training not being compulsory after the age of 40 years
options.C: He must undergo the training only if his office is located in Region 'A'
options.D: He must undergo the training on payment of the prescribed fee

q: In a Central Government office, 84 per cent of the staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi. The correct position regarding notification of the office under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office cannot be notified, as notification requires more than 90 per cent of the staff to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.B: The office cannot be notified, as notification depends on the total number of staff and not on any proportion
options.C: The office can be notified, the prescribed proportion being 80 per cent or more of the staff having acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.D: The office can be notified only during Hindi Pakhwada

q: An employee does noting and drafting in Hindi of 11,000 words during a year and claims consideration for a cash award under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: He is not eligible, the prescribed minimum being 50,000 words in a year
options.B: He becomes eligible for consideration for the cash award, the prescribed minimum being at least 10,000 words of noting and drafting in Hindi in a year
options.C: He is eligible only if he has also passed the Pragya examination with 70 per cent or more marks
options.D: He is eligible only if his office is notified under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 347 of the Constitution, where the President directs that a language spoken by a substantial proportion of the population of a State shall be officially recognised, such recognition may be for the whole or any part of the State and for such purposes as he may specify.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

1. The language Sindhi was included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution by the Constitution (21st Amendment) Act, 1967.

Consider the following statements:
1. Odia was accorded the status of a 'classical language' by the Government of India in the year 2013.
2. Hindi Pakhwada (Hindi Fortnight) is observed every year in Central Government offices and Railways from 14th September to 28th September.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Quarterly Progress Report on the progressive use of Hindi is required to be sent by a Central Government office every quarter.
2. The Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar of the Department of Official Language was earlier known as the Indira Gandhi Rajbhasha Puraskar.

Consider the following statements:
1. World Hindi Day (Vishwa Hindi Diwas) commemorates the adoption of Hindi as the Official Language of the Union by the Constituent Assembly on 14th September, 1949.

Consider the following statements:
1. Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali were added to the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution by the Constitution (92nd Amendment) Act, 2003.
2. Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali were added to the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution by the Constitution (71st Amendment) Act, 1992.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Under the Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi, the target fixed for noting on files in Hindi is 30 per cent.
2. The Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield is awarded on Indian Railways to the best (Adarsh) Division for excellence in implementation of the Official Language Policy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Article 350A of the Constitution provides for the appointment of a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities by the President.

1. Article 344 of the Constitution provides for the constitution of an Official Language Commission at the expiration of five years from the commencement of the Constitution, and thereafter at the expiration of ten years from such commencement.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. A cash award for passing the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is admissible on securing 90 per cent or more marks.
2. Personal pay equal to one increment, admissible to an employee on passing the prescribed Hindi examination, is admissible for a period of 24 months.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

1. The Official Languages (Use for Official Purposes of the Union) Rules, 1976 apply to the whole of India, including the State of Tamil Nadu.

1. Under Section 8 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act vests in the Central Government.

Consider the following statements:
1. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands is placed in Region 'A'.
2. Under the Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi, at least 25 per cent of the amount spent on purchase of books for office libraries should be spent on Hindi books.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 120 of the Constitution, business in Parliament can be transacted only in Hindi.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. In-service Hindi training was made compulsory for Central Government employees by the Presidential Order of 1960.
2. Hindi workshops (Hindi Karyashala) are organised in Central Government offices primarily to give employees practical training to do their noting, drafting and other official work in Hindi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Parangat course under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is the final prescribed course for clerical (ministerial) staff.
2. The office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities functions under the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Prabodh course from the Praveen course under the Hindi Teaching Scheme?

options.A: Prabodh corresponds broadly to the middle (Class VIII) level, while Praveen corresponds broadly to the primary (Class V) level
options.B: Both the courses correspond broadly to the Matriculation (Class X) level
options.C: Prabodh corresponds broadly to the primary (Class V) level and is the first prescribed course, while Praveen corresponds broadly to the middle (Class VIII) level and is undergone after Prabodh
options.D: Prabodh is the final prescribed course for clerical staff, while Praveen is a course in Hindi stenography

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Central Hindi Directorate from the Central Hindi Training Institute in the Hindi teaching arrangements?

options.A: The correspondence courses in Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya are conducted by the Central Hindi Training Institute, while the examinations are conducted by the Central Hindi Directorate
options.B: The correspondence courses in Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya are conducted by the Central Hindi Directorate, while the Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya examinations are conducted by the Central Hindi Training Institute
options.C: Both the correspondence courses and the examinations are conducted by the Central Hindi Directorate
options.D: Both the correspondence courses and the examinations are conducted by the Central Hindi Training Institute

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Hindi Diwas from World Hindi Day (Vishwa Hindi Diwas)?

options.A: Hindi Diwas is observed on 14th September to commemorate the adoption of Hindi as the Official Language of the Union in the year 1949, while World Hindi Day is observed on 10th January to commemorate the first World Hindi Conference held at Nagpur in January 1975
options.B: Both are observed on 14th September, Hindi Diwas in India and World Hindi Day abroad
options.C: Hindi Diwas commemorates the first World Hindi Conference, while World Hindi Day commemorates the adoption of Hindi as the Official Language of the Union
options.D: Hindi Diwas is observed on 10th January, while World Hindi Day is observed on 14th September

q: Which one of the following statements relating to the bilingual and trilingual display and publication requirements in Central Government offices is FALSE?

options.A: Manuals, codes, forms and other procedural literature are printed and published in diglot form, i.e., in Hindi and English
options.B: Name boards, designation boards and sign boards at railway stations and offices are displayed in three languages — the regional language, Hindi and English
options.C: Rubber stamps used in a Central Government office may be prepared in English only, stamps being internal stationery of the office
options.D: Advertisements of a Central Government office are released in Hindi and English (bilingual), i.e., in both Hindi and English newspapers

q: Which one of the following statements relating to the language of correspondence and noting in Central Government offices is FALSE?

options.A: A letter received in Hindi by a Central Government office must be replied to in Hindi
options.B: An employee who records his noting on a file in Hindi cannot be required to furnish an English translation of that noting
options.C: Communications from a Ministry or Department of the Central Government to its attached and subordinate offices situated in Region 'A' shall be in Hindi in such proportion as the Central Government may determine from time to time
options.D: A letter received in English by a Central Government office must invariably be replied to in Hindi

q: Which one of the following statements relating to the reporting and monitoring of the progressive use of Hindi is FALSE?

options.A: The Quarterly Progress Report on the progressive use of Hindi is required to be sent by a Central Government office every quarter
options.B: The Quarterly Progress Report on the progressive use of Hindi is submitted by a Central Government office directly to the President of India
options.C: The Quarterly Progress Report on the progressive use of Hindi is submitted by a Central Government office to its controlling office / administrative Ministry or Department
options.D: To ensure that the documents specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 are invariably issued in both Hindi and English, certain points in a Central Government office, such as the despatch section, are designated as 'Check Points'

options.D: No cash award is admissible below 60 per cent marks

q: An employee passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 63 per cent marks. The cash award admissible to him is:

options.C: No cash award is admissible below 70 per cent marks

options.B: He fails, the prescribed speed being 90 words per minute
options.C: His result is withheld, speed alone being insufficient for passing
options.D: He fails, the prescribed speed being 100 words per minute

q: An employee passes the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 93 per cent marks. In this case:

options.A: A cash award is admissible to him, the prescribed threshold for the stenography examination being 88 per cent or more marks
options.B: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 95 per cent marks
options.C: A cash award is admissible only if he also passes the Hindi typewriting examination
options.D: He becomes entitled to personal pay for a period of 24 months

q: An employee passes the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 84 per cent marks. In this case:
